problems.issue: The bore between the two 6001 seats is only 14 mm (bearing_seat through= with the default shaft_clear 1.0, so d/2+1 = 7 mm radius). A 6001 inner ring face reaches out to about 16.7 mm diameter (d1). retainer.py even says 'inner race land ~12-16.7 mm'. So the fixed printed shoulder at z=28 and z=45.3 touches the TURNING inner race of both bearings from r=7 to about r=8.35. When the retainer's M3 screw clamps the stack, part of that clamp force goes straight through the inner rings into the plastic shoulder instead of through the balls. The turntable then binds or scrapes against an MG996R that
problems.fix: Pass shaft_clear so the through-bore is about 19-20 mm diameter: larger than inner-race d1 16.7 plus 1 mm, and well under outer-race D2 about 24.4, so the shoulder still carries the outer races. For example bearing_seat(..., shaft_clear=4.0) on the lower seat and keep through= as is. Do the same on the upper seat's 1 mm through-cut.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: There is no cable path (docs/ENGINEERING.md section 10: 'Cable path from base to wrist that survives the full motion range'). DESIGN.md only adds 15-20 cm extension leads to the BOM. Four servo leads (shoulder, elbow, wrist, grip) have to cross the +/-90 deg yaw joint. The spindle is solid, nothing on the turntable or base guides them, and the 36:24 gear mesh (z 53.9-61.9, behind the tower) is fully open right below the platform edge where the leads will hang. A lead caught in the mesh will stall the yaw servo or get cut. The elbow, wrist and grip leads have no clips or channels along the fork
problems.fix: Make the spindle hollow (for example 12 mm OD, 6 mm bore, still checked with FEA) or add a cable slot through the platform at the yaw axis. Run the leads down through the tower to a side exit in the base, or add a guarded cable loop at the back with a printed cover over the gear mesh. Add tie-wrap slots or clip bosses on the webs of each fork. Declare the paths as keep-outs or channel_clear and ch
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: turntable_fea does not test the real load. (1) The torque_nmm loads sit on the yoke foot screw sites (x = -29, -14, 10), but their axis is at x = 0. kerf/fea.py applies a torque as traction d x (x - o), so the screw sites, which are not centred on the axis, get a net force. The report shows applied_force_n z = +24.8 N (UP), when the case should be about 12.8 N DOWN, and applied moment 913 N*mm instead of 1280. (2) The tipping moment is underestimated. DESIGN.md uses 0.64 kg x 0.10 m = 0.63 N*m, but the distal arm plus payload alone gives 7.8 kg*cm about the shoulder plus about 0.45 kg x 2.5 cm
problems.fix: Model the load the way it really enters: either apply a resultant force and moment at the yoke feet as matching force pairs (+F/-F at the front and rear screws, plus the downward weight), or apply the torque about the screw-pattern centroid. Fix the turntable at the bearing seats with bearing_n loads on the spindle at each bearing, not as a rigid box over the whole spindle. Use the real 2x tipping
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: Same torque-on-offset-sites effect: yoke_r_fea reports applied_force_n z = +21.3 N, but the spec is -5.9 N. The tab screws are centred 10 mm from the output axis. The real reaction of the servo case to a stall torque is a pure couple, with no net force on the screws. The result passes with a lot of margin, but the load case is not what the 'why' text says.
problems.fix: Apply the stall reaction as a couple about the tab-screw centroid (a couple acts the same about any point), plus the 5.9 N separately. Also worth an engine fix: report or remove the net force a torque_nmm load adds when the axis is not centred on its sites.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: upper_arm_fea fixes BOTH plates rigidly at the shoulder. In reality plate B is pinned on the yoke_l pivot and passes its moment to plate A through the two 4 mm webs, so the load path through the webs is not tested. The applied load is also 19.2 N in total, against the intended 2 x 3.87 = 7.7 N (force_n per site x 4 sites). That is conservative, so it does not change the pass, but the load case is not the one described.
problems.fix: Fix only the shoulder horn screw sites, and hold plate B against radial movement at the pivot only. Divide the per-site forces by the number of sites.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: All servo tab screws are thread-formed into PETG (kind='tap'). They carry the joint torque reaction, and the servos will come off at least once (DESIGN.md says to test-fit, and replacement is likely). ENGINEERING.md section 7 asks for heat-set inserts for parts that carry load or are taken apart more than once. Applies to yoke_r, upper_arm, forearm, gripper and base as well.
problems.fix: Either use heat-set inserts where the 1.6 mm catalog minimum wall to the window allows (it does for the DS32xx windows), or note in DESIGN.md why tapped holes are accepted here: the screws are loaded mainly in shear, and the build notes should say 'do not overtighten'.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The grip is a single swinging finger against a fixed jaw. At 55 deg open, the gap measured square to the jaw at the tcp (45 mm from the pivot) is about 39.5 mm. A 40 mm object therefore fits only at the fingertips, and the swing pushes it along the jaw. The finger closes to a 0.5 mm gap, so holding any object means the MG996R sits at stall continuously.
problems.fix: Allow grip to about 65 deg, or move the fixed jaw outward by about 5 mm. In DESIGN.md, state the grip force at the tcp and that the controller must back off from stall once it has hold of an object.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew any part (its own part was not touched)

problems.issue: The fixed-jaw post stands along gripper +Y, which is print Z when printed with print_rot [90,0,0]. The 18.4 N jaw load bends it ACROSS layers, but gripper_fea judges it as xy with SF 2. The peak of 9.9 MPa is still under the 13 MPa z-allowable at SF 3, so it does not fail, but the declared direction is wrong for the weakest feature.
problems.fix: Use direction z with SF 3 for gripper_fea (it still passes), and add a fillet of at least 2 mm where the post meets the palm.

problems.issue: The mast is a 61 mm column 8 x 10 mm on a 28 x 10 x 5 mm foot, held by 2 M3 that both lie on the y = 0 line. A sideways (+/-Y) pull on the bundle is reacted only over the 5 mm half-width of the foot, so a 20 N snag at the top (61 mm) puts about 240 N of prying into one insert. At |yaw| near 90 the bundle tension acts exactly in that direction, because the base post is then off to the side of the turntable. The column-to-foot inside corner is sharp (ENGINEERING.md section 5: >= 1 mm fillet on a load path).
problems.fix: Widen the foot to about 22 mm in Y and use 3-4 screws spread in both X and Y (or move the two screws to (-10, +/-8)). Add a 2 mm fillet or a small gusset where the column meets the foot.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The cable post is a 126 mm upright cantilever (10 x 26 mm) printed with its layers across its bending direction. It has a sharp root at the plate and the PCA9685 is screwed to it. Stress from the bundle is low (about 1.5 MPa per 5 N), but a knock or a yank on the bundle bends it at the weakest across-layer section, a single sharp corner. DESIGN.md part list says the base is 88 g; report.json says 130.5 g (ENGINEERING.md section 11 requires the mass budget within 10 %).
problems.fix: Add a 3-4 mm root fillet or two small triangular gussets at the post foot (front and back). Update the part-list masses from report.json.

problems.fix: Cut matching vent openings in the -Y wall at the slot positions (or stand the wall off 1 mm with ribs and keep only the screw boss in contact). Make the tie anchor a bridge or loop standing on the floor (a 4 x 2 mm tunnel under a 2 mm strap), not a through-slot.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: The IR-drop rows leave out resistances that are in the catalog or certain to be there. The 5 A ATO fuse has cold_resistance_ohm 0.01785 (about 45 mV at 2.5 A). Each servo lead also has the plug-to-extension contact (two 0.1 in contacts in the loop). The servo's own 300 mm lead is assumed to be 22 AWG, but the catalog has no gauge for any servo's lead (MG996R pigtails are often thinner). The wrist and grip peak rows (4.851 V against 4.8) have 51 mV of margin, which these effects use up. The rows are soft (stall transient), so this is not a failure, but the stated margin is optimistic.
problems.fix: Engine: add the fuse's cold_resistance_ohm, and the fuse holder's lead length at its 16 AWG gauge, to the run's loop resistance in electrical.py (the data is already in the catalog). Add a sourced lead gauge to the servo catalog entries, or treat the own-lead part as the thinner of 22/26 AWG. With 5.5 V available from the SVR, trimming to 5.4 V would restore the margin (all servos are rated to at

problems.issue: The docstring still says 'foot and column flush (10 mm) so it needs no support'. The foot is now 26 mm wide in Y with the 10 mm column centred on it, so lying on its side (print_rot [90,0,0]) the 61 mm column stands 8 mm off the bed along its whole length on support (12.6 % support surface). The support side of the column is left rough. DESIGN.md has the correct description.
problems.fix: Correct the docstring. Optionally, flush the column with one long side of the foot (shift X_COL's Y offset, foot y -5..21), or split the foot into a separate pad, so the column lies on the bed with no support.

problems.issue: Carried over and accepted: the Nano, the 4 WAGO splices and the 5 inline fuse holders are loose on the desk behind the base. DESIGN.md now tells the builder to case the Nano and screw the supply down. The supply's plan-view M3 holes are only 3 mm deep, so screwing it to a desk top needs a thin board or long screws from below.
problems.fix: None required. A small printed electronics tray on the rear pad (Nano posts, WAGO clips, fuse-holder slots) would make the desk layout tidy and short-proof.

problems.issue: The SVR hole (d 8 at x 5.1, y 9.6) and the LED hole (d 3.5 at x 11.1, y 9.9) are 6.0 mm apart centre to centre. That leaves a 0.26 mm web between them (6.007 - 4 - 1.75), less than one 0.4 mm extrusion line. It will print as a ragged sliver or not at all, and the two holes merge into one 8 x 12 mm slot. This is still finger-safe (8 mm wide is less than the 12 mm IEC test finger) and the mains pins are 50 mm or more away, so it is cosmetic and robustness only.
problems.fix: Leave at least 1.2 mm web: cut the LED hole at 2.5 mm, or move it to x 12 (the LED still shows, given the ±1 mm case tolerance). Alternatively, cut one deliberate rounded slot over both.

Separately, in the print orientation (standing on the end wall) the bridge block's -X face is a 6 x 5 mm flat overhang that sticks out 5 mm from a vertical wall. Report overh
problems.fix: Reword the note: feed the DC pairs out of the exit and tie them to the bridge with the hood held beside the supply, then lower or slide the hood on and fit the side screw. Optionally, chamfer the bridge block's -X underside at 45 degrees.

This may mean starting the widened pocket at x = -47 so the cut opens into it. Option B: make both the exit and the

problems.issue: base.py hard-codes the cable boss protrusion as 6.6 mm (boss_x1 = xc + L/2 + 6.6 + 0.6). It still clears, but it goes against the rule that purchased-part dimensions come from the catalog.
problems.fix: Read d['cable_boss_protrusion'] (or the catalog key) instead of 6.6, keep the +0.6 clearance, and re-check.

problems.issue: In the upright print, the shelf underside is the face the tab tops clamp against, and it is printed over support across the open pocket. The access ceiling at z_shelf - 0.5 (44 x 13 mm) is also supported. A rough supported face under the tabs can let the servo rock slightly once the screws are snug.

problems.issue: Round-5 items verified. The pot hole is now 7 mm and the LED hole 2.5 mm (web 6.007 - 3.5 - 1.25 = 1.26 mm), and the two holes show separate in part_psu_hood_top.png. The optional 45 degree chamfer on the bridge's -X underside was not done, so the 6 x 5 mm overhang will still sag slightly.

problems.issue: For the record: at the new crash-case SF 3, upper_arm_stall_fea p99.9 is 13.42 MPa against a 16 MPa limit (a margin of 1.19). The DS32xx tab holes are still UNVERIFIED in the catalog.

After the ENG-6 perimeter-aware mass change, report.json and bom.md give upper_arm 64.8 g (was 47), forearm 55.4 (40), gripper 29.4 (22), finger 5.0 (4), base 175 (134), and arm_mass 791 g (DESIGN says 693). Use upper_arm_fea 2 x 4.11 N and 2 x 4.46 kg*cm = 875 N*mm, forearm 2 x 2.95 N and 2 x 1.91 kg*cm, the yoke and turntable weight from the current turntable-borne mass, and the tipping moment from the current shoulder torque. Better still, derive them in layout.py or an expression from the masses so they cannot go sta

I confirmed it in the STL at x -50..-38, and it is visible in part_base_sheet.png FRONT. Nothing uses it now. problems.issue: The yaw lead bends hard at the grommet. The pocket's +X end wall is at x -27.4 (STL), only 0.6 mm past the catalog's 7.0 mm cable-boss envelope (case end -35.0, envelope tip -28.0). The real MG996R wires leave the boss heading +X, so they must turn down against that wall almost at the grommet, and during the push-up from below they drag along it. The route still works because the pocket is open below and the wires are thin, but it is a kink point at the strain relief. Also, nothing holds the lead in the groove while the base is turned over onto the desk.
problems.fix: Give the end wall 2-3 mm more clearance at boss height, or chamfer the wall's lower inside edge. In DESIGN.md step 2, say to pre-bend the lead downward at the boss before pushing the servo up, and to hold the lead in the groove with a strip of tape while turning the base over.
problems.resolved_how: first commit after the finding that redrew its part

problems.issue: Round-6 route item, only partly fixed. pwr_yaw and sig_yaw now pass base.yaw_boss (-30.4, 0, 13), but the engine still adds the servo origin (-55.2, 0, 27.8) as the last point, so the drawn lead still ends inside the MG996R case (report.json electrical.wires points).
problems.fix: Engine: end a lead at the servo's cable-boss point (a 'lead' joint on the servo proxy) instead of its origin. This is general and would fix every project.

problems.issue: base_fea applies about 80 % of its stated tipping-moment load. Both the why text and DESIGN.md (Architecture: 'two 6001 bearings 25 mm apart'; yaw-bearing hand check '~25 mm spacing'; Strength table '+-72 N bearing couple (2 x 0.90 N*m over the 25 mm seat spacing)'; base.py docstring) assume 25 mm between the bearings. layout.py actually gives z_blo = 20 and z_bhi = z_tt - B = 40.5. The bearing centres are at z 24 and 44.5, so they are 20.5 mm apart. The base_fea cylinders sit on exactly those seats. +-72 N x 20.5 mm = 1476 N*mm, and the report shows applied_moment_nmm My = 1463. The static mo
problems.fix: In base_fea set bearing_n to [91, -34, 0] on the upper seat and [-91, 0, 0] on the lower (1.86 N*m / 20.5 mm). Better, write it as an expression: 2 x the tipping moment / (z_bhi - z_blo). Correct the spacing to 20.5 mm in the why text, in DESIGN.md (Architecture, the hand check giving +-45 N static per bearing, the Strength table) and in the base.py docstring. Rebuild and update the base_fea row.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: The tipping-moment arithmetic is slightly low, and its wording is wrong. The turntable_fea why says 'the arm weight 2.5 cm behind it', but the shoulder axis is 25 mm AHEAD of the yaw axis (x_sh = +25), which is why that term adds to the moment. DESIGN's hand check gives '8.2 kg*cm + 0.6 kg x 2.5 cm ~ 0.90 N*m', but that sum is 0.95 N*m. The correct figure (0.487 kg beyond the shoulder) is ~0.93 N*m. So 2x = 1.86 N*m, while the net applied moment is 1.805 N*m (report My), which is 1.94x. Not material at 3.9 vs 13 MPa.
problems.fix: Use 2 x 0.93 N*m: couples of ~1010 N*mm each, giving a net of ~1.86 N*m after the 13.8 N at x -11. Change 'behind' to 'ahead' and fix the DESIGN hand-check arithmetic. The same 0.93 N*m feeds the base_fea fix above.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: The load 'why' texts leave out the servo body that hangs on each link's far end. The 'rounded up for leads/screws' margin silently absorbs it. Upper arm: 359 g beyond the elbow + the el_servo's 60 g on the upper arm's tabs = 418.8 g, so 2x = 8.22 N against 8.4 applied, which leaves ~18 g for leads and screws. Forearm: 245.4 g + wr_servo 55 g = 300.4 g, so 2x = 5.89 N against 6.0 applied, which leaves ~5 g, less than the wrist and grip leads that run beyond the wrist. Yokes: 486.6 g + the 60 g shoulder servo on yoke_r. Every case still covers 2x of the hardware plus the payload, but the stated
problems.fix: Restate each why as (servo on the link + everything beyond the joint + payload) x 2 x g, plus an explicit lead allowance. Raise the forearm to 3.1 N per site (6.2 N) so that ~10 g of lead is covered.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: Several holes print horizontally but are cut round without compensation (ENGINEERING.md s4: 'Horizontal holes print oval: use teardrop or add +0.2 mm'). upper_arm, forearm and gripper print on edge (print_rot [90,0,0]), so every hole along the link's Z axis is horizontal on the bed. The free pivot holes have teardrops, but the servo-tab self-tap pilots (servo_mount kind='tap', no teardrop) are the 2.6 mm vertical PETG pilot rather than the catalog's horizontal pilot, which is +0.18 mm. The heat-set pivot insert holes (pin_hole fit='heatset': sh_pivot in upper_arm, el_pivot in forearm, wr_pivot
problems.fix: Pass teardrop=<print-up direction> (iface.print_up_deg) to servo_mount and to the heat-set pin_hole calls in upper_arm.py, forearm.py and gripper.py, as yoke_r/yoke_l already do for their foot holes.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: DESIGN.md's Strength table gives base_fea deflection as 0.11 mm, but report.json has 0.129 mm. The turntable row says 0.23 mm against a report value of 0.239, which rounds to 0.24. Stale by a small amount. Both are still under the 0.3 mm limit.
problems.fix: Update the base_fea row to 0.13 mm and the turntable_fea row to 0.24 mm.

problems.issue: In print orientation (print_rot [90,0,0], out/parts/gripper.stl) the lowest geometry is the bottom of the two r = link_h/2 = 17 mm wrist discs. The side-plate rectangles only reach y = -6 (Rectangle(x_end, 12.0)), so the plates' 80 mm lower edges and the palm start 11 mm above the bed. Bed contact is about 36 mm2 of tessellated cylinder: two line contacts on round 7 mm discs. The largest downward flat face (897 mm2, the plate lower edges) is printed entirely on support. The engine warns 'only 0 mm2 sits on the bed against a 1669 mm2 flat face'. The gripper.py docstring ('Printed standing on it
problems.fix: Give the side plates a flat lower edge at the disc tangent. In gripper.py, extend each plate profile down to y = -r (for example Rectangle from y = -r to +6 over at least the first ~25 mm), then rise at 45 degrees back to y = -6 so the rest of the edge is self-supporting. Alternatively take the full 80 mm down to y = -r if the mass budget allows (about +12 g; arm_mass is 791 of 900 g). Then re-run

problems.issue: Not seen in round 9 (engine check added after it): the horn clearance holes (sh_horn on upper_arm, el_horn on forearm, wr_horn on gripper) and the cable_mast and psu_side clearance holes print horizontal without a teardrop. These are 3.4 mm clearance holes for M3, so a 0.1-0.2 mm sag at the top still passes a screw.
problems.fix: Pass teardrop=iface.print_up_deg(ctx, loc) to those horn_mount/bolt_pattern calls, as already done for the tab pilots and pivot inserts. Otherwise, add a DESIGN.md note to run a 3.4 mm drill through them.

problems.issue: Not seen in round 9: the engine warns that base_fea's fixed boxes hold none of base's fastener sites. The four 12 x 12 mm boxes do sit on the underside around the four M4 desk holes, which is the real restraint. The warning fires because those holes are cut with iface.hole and not registered as sites. The FEA setup is right, but the warning stays.
problems.fix: Cut the desk holes with a site-registering call (bolt_pattern with group 'desk') so the check can see them, or note in DESIGN.md that the boxes are the M4 desk-screw footprints.

problems.issue: DESIGN.md 'Use notes' tells the IK to reject poses whose tcp or wrist pivot is below z = 15 mm, assuming the jaws are about 12 mm below the tcp line. The grip MG996R hangs under the palm about 31 mm below the tcp. I checked a pose grid with shoulder/elbow in 20 degree steps and wrist at -75/0/75, keeping only poses that pass the documented rule. At shoulder -20 / elbow 0 / wrist 0 (tcp z = 25 mm) the grip servo's lowest point is at z = -6.4 mm, and at shoulder -60 / elbow 60 it is at -2.9 mm. So the rule as written lets the grip servo case hit the desk. The stall FEA covers the printed parts,
problems.fix: In DESIGN.md Use notes, base the desk limit on the lowest point of the gripper and grip servo, not the tcp: reject any pose where the tcp is below about z = 45 mm with the wrist horizontal, or compute the grip servo's bottom corner in the IK and keep it above z = 10 mm.

problems.issue: 11.1 % of the surface still prints on support: the palm underside (11 mm above the bed between the plates) and the fixed jaw. This is documented in DESIGN.md and the docstring, and it is the right trade-off for an on-edge print that keeps the plates' bending stress along the layers.
problems.fix: None required. Optionally chamfer the jaw's underside at 45 degrees to cut its support.
